class.name: FellowLightning3D
class.brief_description: Lightning: strikes around the camera that flash over the scene, with a glowing bolt and a lit cloud (FellowEngine).
class.description: Strikes come at random times ([member strikes_per_minute]) and distances ([member distance_range]) around the current camera, or when [method strike] is called. A strike is two to four return strokes, each a flash that decays in about 40 ms: a [DirectionalLight3D] shining from the bolt's direction lights the scene (with [member shadows]), the bolt — a branching channel of [member cloud_height], built when it strikes and turned to the camera — glows, and the cloud above it lights up. Bloom makes the bolt's glow. The strikes are a function of [member seed] and [member time], so the same clock gives the same storm. [signal struck] gives the bolt's foot and its distance, for the thunder: it arrives [code]distance / 343[/code] seconds later. Decision record [code]docs/decisions/0129-lightning.md[/code].

method.name: get_flash
method.description: The strike's brightness now, from 0 to 1 (0 between strikes).

method.name: get_flash_light
method.description: The internal light of the flashes (visible only while one lasts).

method.name: is_striking
method.description: Whether a strike is in progress.

method.name: strike
method.description: Strikes now, [param distance] metres from the camera (negative: at random within [member distance_range]) towards [param azimuth_degrees] (0: +X, 90: +Z; below -360: at random). Returns the bolt's foot.

members.member: The bolt's brightness at a stroke's peak.
The bolt's width as seen from the camera, in radians (0.006: about 6 pixels at 1080p with a 55 degree view).
The height of the cloud the bolts come from, in metres above the node.
How brightly the volumetric clouds ([code]rendering/fellow/post/clouds/enabled[/code]) glow around a flash, as much as they are opaque, by how near the view passes to it (0: not at all).
The colour of the flash and the bolt.
The nearest and farthest a random strike falls from the camera, in metres (uniformly over the ring's area).
The flash light's energy at a stroke's peak for a strike 1 km away (nearer brighter, by the inverse of the distance, 0.3 to 2.5 times).
The storm: with the same seed and clock, the same strikes.
How often it strikes at random (0: only when [method strike] is called).
If [code]true[/code], the node's clock advances with the frames; otherwise set [code]time[/code] yourself.

signal.name: struck
signal.description: A strike began: [param position] is the bolt's foot, [param distance] its distance from the camera in metres.
